shot.prose: The page opens with a confident, oversized hero heading — "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" — set in a heavy serif-adjacent bold that makes the hierarchy immediately clear at a glance; there is no ambiguity about what matters most here. Below the heading, the body paragraph reads comfortably against the light gray background, and the inline `import` chip (dark fill, light text) earns its place as a concise visual cue without pulling focus from the prose. The stat cards introduce a 2-column grid that starts cleanly — "EXECUTABLE LINES / 714" and "GZIPPED, WITH CSS / 21 KB" sit side by side with consistent padding and white card surfaces that read clearly as distinct panels against the gray page. However, the fifth card, "CONFIG FILES / 0," breaks that rhythm by sitting alone in the left column with a large blank void to its right; this reads as an accident of an odd item count rather than deliberate asymmetry, and the empty right half of that row is the most visually disruptive element on the screen. The card label text — "EXECUTABLE LINES," "BUILD STEPS," etc. — is uppercase, small, and light gray; while readable at normal viewing distance, it sits close to the contrast floor and could fatigue on low-brightness screens. The paragraph beneath the cards switches to a teal-blue color ("Measured from a clean checkout — Versus has the method…") which differs from the black body text above; the "Versus" link is clearly underlined in orange, but the surrounding sentence being in a different hue from the rest of the body creates an inconsistency that could read as a mistake rather than an intentional callout. Vertical spacing between the navbar and the hero headline is generous to the point of feeling loose — that gap above "A no-build…" is noticeably large for a 390px mobile viewport where every pixel of vertical rhythm counts. Alignment of the left card edges is consistent and the horizontal gutters between columns appear even. The hamburger icon in the top right is standard and reachable, but the nav bar itself almost disappears into the page background since both are near-white with no visible separator.

shot.prose: The page is a mobile-width framework catalog at scroll 0. The overall skeleton — navbar, "UI" title, tabs, intro paragraph, filter list, card grid — is coherent and follows a logical reading order from top to bottom. The orange "EVERYTHING" row reads immediately as the active filter, giving the filter list strong hierarchy and making it easy to orient. However, the gap between the last filter row ("MARKS") and the "SURFACES" section heading below it is noticeably larger than the gaps between the filter rows themselves, creating a jarring pause that makes the two regions feel unrelated rather than connected. The "View" card renders on a white surface against the gray page background, so it reads as a proper card, but its interior has an unusual amount of vertical dead space — the subtitle text sits near the top and the card bottom edge is far below, leaving the lower half of the card empty. The "CORE" label inside that card is rendered in a light gray at very small size; against the white card background, it's the lowest-contrast element on the visible page and would be hard to read for many users. The placeholder text in the search field reads "Search 19," which is ambiguous — it seems to mean "search across 19 items," but a casual reader will parse it as a fixed label or a pre-filled value rather than a result count, which is confusing UX. At the very bottom of the viewport a secondary toolbar appears with a small orange "NEW" chip, an "IMPORT" label, a "Filter modules…" input, and two icon buttons; these touch targets are very compact on a 390 px screen and the toolbar appears to be cut off, so its full affordance is unclear. The tab row (OVERVIEW, API, DOCS, FILES) aligns cleanly left-to-right with the underline active indicator on OVERVIEW, though the tab labels are uppercase and tightly kerned — functional but slightly cold. Alignment across the search field, filter rows, and section heading is consistent, which helps the vertical rhythm. There is no imagery or iconography above the fold beyond the logo mark, making the page feel entirely textual — not broken, but the catalog cards could benefit from a visual element to differentiate them at a glance.

shot.prose: The "Web" heading anchors the page cleanly — its weight and size immediately establish where you are, and the grey background gives the white cards a legible lift. The two cards (Navigation, Layout) read as surfaces and their small icons plus bold titles give them a consistent internal structure, though the icons are so small (roughly 16 px glyphs in a corner) that they contribute almost nothing to visual character and feel like decoration that hasn't earned its place. The gap between the bottom edge of the Layout card and the "/framework/ is the reference" paragraph below is noticeably larger than the gap between the two cards — this creates a visual pause that reads more like a page break than a section lead-in, and the connective intent of that paragraph is weakened by the distance. The first explanatory paragraph is the hardest thing to read on the page: a dark-badge `Page`, another dark-badge `Router`, and an orange-underlined "the CSS layers" all interrupt the line in quick succession, chopping what should be a flowing sentence into a punctuation obstacle course. The body text that follows — the second and third paragraphs including "Every demo here is a real `Page` tree…" — sits on the raw grey without any framing surface, while the content above it has white cards; this mix of framed and unframed prose in the same scroll creates a slight inconsistency. Alignment is solid: the card body copy, the prose paragraphs, and the heading all share a common left rail. The orange-underlined "Navigation" and "Layout" at the very bottom read immediately as links, which is good, but they use the same orange underline style as "the CSS layers" inline above, which is a code-layer label — the shared styling blurs whether something is a navigational link or a concept label.

shot.prose: The page is a single-column documentation view for a tool called DesignTool, read top-to-bottom as nav → heading → tab bar → code block → prose, which is the right structural order for 390 px. The "DesignTool" heading dominates at a glance and the red rule beneath it anchors the title clearly; hierarchy is solid. The active tab "OVERVIEW" carries a visible underline indicator that distinguishes it from the other two tabs, though "TASTE" sits so close to the right viewport edge that it has almost no right padding and could be difficult to hit reliably as a touch target. The dark code block is the most significant problem: both lines of code are visibly truncated at the right — "Desig" and ".page.active-" are cut off with no ellipsis, no fade, and no visible horizontal-scroll affordance, so a reader can't tell whether scrolling is even possible. The vertical gap between the tab bar's bottom edge and the top of that code block is notably tight — there's barely a sliver of whitespace and the block feels pinched against the navigation. Prose body text on white is legible, but the two orange-underline links (`vision-baseline` and `tier-calibration`) may be borderline for contrast against white without a bold weight to compensate. Near the bottom of the visible area, three dark inline code badges (`width-used`, `repetition`, `heading-offset`) cluster within a single sentence and create a staccato rhythm that interrupts readability; the density feels higher than the surrounding prose warrants. The warning callout (⚠ icon + bold sentence) works well as a visual interruption to signal a critical note. No imagery appears, which is fine for reference documentation, but a single diagram of the tool's output format would give the code block meaningful context.

shot.prose: The page is well-structured: a white sidebar hugging the left, a light-gray content field to its right, and prose + stat cards occupying a centered column. The heading "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" reads instantly as the dominant element — the weight and size drop-off to the subtitle paragraph is steep in a good way, and hierarchy lands in one glance. The four stat cards in the first row ("714 / EXECUTABLE LINES", "21 KB / GZIPPED WITH CSS", "0 / BUILD STEPS", "0 / RUNTIME DEPS") are evenly sized, and the large bold numerals give them satisfying visual punch. However, the fifth card "CONFIG FILES / 0" sits alone in a second row with roughly three card-widths of empty gray to its right, producing a clear orphan that makes the stat grid look unfinished rather than intentional. The white cards on a light-gray page background are readable, but their differentiation relies almost entirely on a thin card border — any rendering context that softens that edge could let them float unframed. The inline `import` dark-chip in the subtitle text is a clever typographic device and earns its contrast without fighting the prose. The dark code block near the bottom gives the lower visible region a solid anchor. Down in the bottom-left corner, a settings gear and a muted gray circle sit side by side with no labels; the circle especially has no visible affordance — its purpose is completely opaque at this scroll position. The top four sidebar entries ("Start here", "AI", "FAQ", "Versus") sit above "CORE" without their own section label, making it unclear whether they belong to a tier or are just orphaned links compared to the labeled groups below.

shot.prose: The page is well-structured overall — a left sidebar with clear section labels, a tabbed content area, and prose that reads in a natural column width. The "DesignTool" page heading is large and anchors the hierarchy immediately, and the orange underline on the active "OVERVIEW" tab is a clean, unambiguous active-state indicator. The dark code block at the top provides a good visual anchor and contrast break before the explanatory prose begins, though it notably stops well short of the right edge of the content column — roughly 20–25% of the content width is bare background to its right, creating a lopsided impression compared with the body text below that fills the full column. The gap between the tab bar's bottom and the top edge of the code block is very small, perhaps 8–10 px, making the content feel like it starts abruptly with almost no breathing room after the navigation chrome. The three inline dark-badge labels — `width-used`, `repetition`, and `heading-offset` — are visually heavy within their paragraph; their solid dark fills interrupt reading flow more aggressively than the surrounding link underlines do, which may be intentional but strains the eye across several lines. At the very bottom of the viewport, the four section cards appear cut off at almost exactly their icon-and-title row, which reveals enough to tease the sections but not enough to convey any meaning — a slightly taller first-screen or a bit less top content would give them more breathing room. The sidebar's gear icon and gray circle in the lower-left corner feel visually orphaned with no label, making their purpose opaque at scroll 0.

shot.prose: The page opens with a bold "Web" heading that anchors hierarchy well — it's the undisputed focal point — but the vertical gap between that heading and the card row below it feels slightly generous relative to the gap between the cards and the body text, creating an uneven rhythm down the left column. The two cards ("Navigation" and "Layout") are cleanly surfaced with white backgrounds and soft borders on a light-grey page, so they read as distinct panels without any floating ambiguity. However, the truncated descriptions inside both cards — "live — and two studies i…" and "Seven principles of arranging a page — eac…" — are cut off mid-word, which damages legibility and looks unfinished rather than intentional; the card height appears sufficient to accommodate at least one more line. The card row only fills roughly the left 40 % of the viewport, leaving the right 60 % as a completely inert grey field with no content, which makes the overall page feel very narrow and poorly balanced for a 1280 px canvas. The prose body text aligns well on its left edge — consistent with the card left edge and the heading — so column alignment is solid throughout. Inline code chips like `/framework/`, `Page`, and `Router` use a dark pill background with light text and render at a noticeably smaller size, which can make them strain against the surrounding body text, especially in the dense first paragraph. The amber/orange underline on links ("Navigation," "Layout," "clicking it") is semantically distinctive but low-contrast against the near-white body text colour, so a fast scan may not immediately register them as interactive. The "Design record" disclosure row at the bottom sits close to the lower edge of the visible area and is separated from the paragraph above by a full horizontal rule, which is a heavier visual weight than the modest `▶` toggle warrants. The page is entirely typographic with no imagery or icons beyond the small compass and grid glyphs inside the card headers, and while that suits a documentation context, the large right-hand void amplifies how text-only the layout feels.

shot.prose: The page presents a component-library index with a left nav, a tab bar, a filter sidebar, and a live-preview grid — the bones are solid and the hierarchy reads quickly. The large "UI" heading and the orange OVERVIEW underline tab nail the immediate orientation, and the orange "EVERYTHING 19" pill establishes the active filter without confusion. However, the "Panel" column in the component grid is glaringly hollow: the "Card" and "Toolbar" columns each carry rich preview content (stat tiles and an accordion Q&A respectively), while the Panel column shows only its label and icon and then leaves a blank rectangle where a preview should be, creating a conspicuous dead zone in an otherwise lively row. The intro paragraph ends on a single word — "it." — hanging alone on its third line, an orphan that weakens the paragraph's visual block and looks unfinished directly below the hero heading. The filter sidebar (search box plus category buttons) shares the same light-gray background as the main content area with no surface of its own, making it feel like it floats rather than occupying a defined panel. The red DELETE button inside the "Delete branch?" showcase card is visually dominant — its intensity pulls the eye to the top-right corner before the more central "View" card, disrupting the intended left-to-right reading flow. Spacing between the three top showcase cards (View / import UI / delete dialog) and the component-label row below (Card / Toolbar / Panel) is noticeably larger than other vertical gaps on the page, which reads like a layout seam rather than intentional breathing room. The "DATA" section label mid-page uses the same all-caps weight as "SURFACES" but appears without a dividing rule or extra leading to clearly signal a new section, so it blends into the flow rather than anchoring a tier. The icon set next to each component name (Card ☐, Toolbar ⇔, Panel ☐, etc.) is consistent and useful for quick scanning — one of the page's stronger details.

The code block carries a dark background and sufficient padding, so it reads as a distinct surface with no ambiguity. At the very bottom of the visible area a gray rectangle appears — presumably the start of the live panel demo — but it carries no visible label or interactive affordance from this scroll position, so it could be mistaken for a loading placeholder. shot.prose: The page is a component-catalog grid laid out in a left-sidebar + main-panel shell. The sidebar navigation is long and densely packed with small items, making it hard to scan at a glance — the section groupings (STYLES, EXTENSIONS) share nearly the same visual weight as the individual items below them, so hierarchy within the sidebar is weak. The introductory paragraph at the top of the main panel spans a wide measure across the content area; at a 3440-pixel viewport that text block would be excessively wide in practice, but even in the screenshot the line length looks uncomfortably long relative to the rest of the page. The component cards are arranged in a five-column grid with reasonable internal gutters, and each card's label (Card, Toolbar, Panel, etc.) sits cleanly above its preview — hierarchy within each cell is clear. The rightmost column (Accordion, Breadcrumbs, Tooltip) shows noticeably more empty white area inside the preview regions compared to the busier cards in columns one through three, creating an uneven density across the row that makes those right-edge cards feel unfinished. The SURFACES, DATA, and FORMS inline section labels that separate the grid rows are tiny and easy to overlook; they are the only landmark that tells a user which category they are browsing within the grid, yet they have no stronger treatment than the component name labels directly below them. The orange "EVERYTHING" pill in the filter bar is the brightest colour on the page and reads as the active filter — that contrast logic is sound. The left sidebar's active item ("UI") appears to be bold or slightly brighter than its siblings, which is a subtle distinction that could be missed, particularly at the small sidebar width visible here. The card preview thumbnails do real work by showing live-rendered examples rather than icons or placeholder images, which is appropriate and earns their space; no card is purely decorative.

Hierarchy within the narrow strip is clear: the heavy "Web" h1 dominates, the cards read as navigational tiles, and the explanatory prose flows underneath — the information order is sound. The body copy explicitly promises "a real Page tree running in a box" but the page shows no demo, screenshot, or diagram above the fold — only the two small card tiles with tiny icons that barely register at this scale.

shot.prose: The page is divided into a narrow left sidebar, a horizontal tab bar, and a single main content column — but on this 3440 px ultrawide viewport the content column occupies only the left-centre third of the screen, leaving roughly 60 % of the horizontal canvas as blank white space with nothing in it, which is the most prominent visual problem at this viewport width. The top tab bar (Overview, Layout Library, Taste, Test Corpus, Site Audit, Knowledge, Widths, Vision Browse, Docs, Files) stretches to maybe 750 px and then stops, sitting orphaned against a sea of white to its right — it does not grow or right-anchor as you would expect at ultrawide. The card grid below the body text — ten labelled tiles for Layout library, Taste, Test corpus, and so on — also stops well short of centre-screen; the tiles are reasonably spaced between themselves but the rightward emptiness makes the whole block feel like it drifted left. Hierarchy is clear within the content column itself: the "DesignTool" logotype and the section heading "This page, measured" are the loudest typographic elements, and the smaller body text and card labels subordinate correctly. The body text is dark on white and fully legible; the amber/orange inline label chips ("align-ok", "missing-step", etc.) are a useful accent colour and readable, though the chip text is small enough that at low pixel density it might strain. The "This page, measured" section at the bottom feels notably sparse — just the heading, a one-line "Analysing…" message, a small "re-run" pill, and a single bullet — there is a lot of breathing room below that bullet before the fold, which, combined with the rightward emptiness, gives the lower half of the viewport an unfinished feeling. The card tiles each carry a faint surface background so they read as distinct panels rather than floating text, though the short description lines inside them are low contrast light-grey on near-white and would be harder to scan at arm's length.

shot.prose: The page opens with a clean navbar — logo icon, wordmark, and a hamburger at the far right — sitting on a very pale-grey ground. The hero heading "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" dominates in heavy black type and reads immediately, though the line break leaves "web" stranded alone before "framework," creating a slightly awkward rhythm that a tighter max-width or a line-break hint could smooth. The `import` badge inline in the paragraph below is dark with reversed text and earns its place as a code callout, though it sits a little heavy against the surrounding body weight. The two-column stat grid is the structural centrepiece: "EXECUTABLE LINES / 714" and "GZIPPED, WITH CSS / 21 KB" share row one neatly, and "BUILD STEPS / 0" and "RUNTIME DEPS / 0" mirror them in row two — but "CONFIG FILES / 0" lands alone in a third row, orphaned in the left column while the right is entirely empty, which breaks the rhythm and reads as an accident rather than a choice. Card spacing and internal padding look consistent across all five cards, and the white card surface against the grey page reads clearly as a lifted element. The paragraph beginning "Measured from a clean checkout" is rendered entirely in blue, making the whole sentence read as one giant hyperlink rather than prose with two embedded links, which is visually confusing and undersells the actual links ("Versus" and the column reference). The `/path/page.js` code badge at the very bottom is cropped mid-sentence by the viewport edge, so the sentence is unresolved within the visible region. Vertical rhythm between sections — hero, paragraph, cards, footer paragraph — feels comfortable rather than cramped.

shot.prose: The page is structured as a left sidebar plus a single content column, and on this 3440 px ultrawide viewport the content column occupies roughly the leftmost 500 px of usable space while the remaining ~2700 px to its right is a flat, featureless grey void — the dominant visual impression is emptiness, not content. The headline "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" is large and bold and immediately reads as the page's main claim, which is correct hierarchy, and the stat cards (714 / 21 KB / 0 / 0 / 0) below it serve as a satisfying visual proof row. The five stat cards are evenly spaced and internally consistent, but their combined row width stops well short of even the narrow text column, so the row feels slightly orphaned beneath the wider heading text. "That's basically it." is rendered in an orange/brand colour that reads as a hyperlink rather than plain body copy — only the absence of underline saves it from being actively confusing. The dark code block offers strong contrast and breaks the text monotony well; syntax colouring is legible against the near-black background. The sidebar's section labels (CORE, STYLES, EXTENSIONS) in small grey caps usefully chunk a long list, though the individual nav items are small enough that they'd be hard to hit precisely on a touch device. "Files" in the sidebar is tinted blue, signalling the active page, but no other selected-state styling is visible, so it's the only orientation cue available. The partially visible clock numerals at the very bottom of the frame (the live panel preview) are enormous and feel dramatically out of scale with the text content just above — the crop makes it impossible to judge intent, but the size jump is jarring even in passing.

shot.prose: The page divides cleanly into a left sidebar and a right content column, and that structure is immediately legible. The hero heading "A no-build, native-ESM web framework" is large, heavy, and lands as the clear focal point in one glance — hierarchy works. The five stat cards (EXECUTABLE LINES, GZIPPED WITH CSS, etc.) form a tidy row with consistent internal padding and border treatment, reading unmistakably as surface tiles rather than floating text. However, the cards auto-size to their content rather than equalising widths, so the first card ("EXECUTABLE LINES / 714") is visibly narrower than the second ("GZIPPED, WITH CSS / 21 KB"), creating a slightly uneven rhythm across the row. The dark code block is well-framed against the light page, and its contrast is strong with no readability concern; the orange-underlined links ("Versus", "column") stand out clearly from body copy. A large expanse of flat gray — roughly 380 px wide — sits idle to the right of the code block and body text from about x ≈ 890 to the viewport edge; whether the narrow content column is intentional or not, that right zone contributes nothing and makes the page feel left-heavy at this viewport width. The gray circle at the very bottom of the sidebar, next to the gear icon, has no label and reads as either a user avatar or a button, but nothing identifies it — a user encountering it for the first time has no affordance cue. The sidebar section labels "CORE" and "STYLES" are small-caps in a light gray that is close in weight to the icon color, which slightly blurs the separation between the category header and the items beneath it.
